facts.text: The Sam Rayburn House State Historic Site, built in 1916, showcases original furnishings and personal belongings of the former Speaker.
Visitors to the 1916 home see candid photographs, vehicles, and farm buildings that illustrate Rayburn’s personal life and political achievements.
The Sam Rayburn House is a National Historic Landmark, preserving the legacy of one of Texas’s most influential legislators.
Sam Rayburn Reservoir, constructed beginning in 1956, was renamed in 1963 to honor the former Speaker’s impact on Texas water resources.
The Sam Rayburn House State Historic Site partners with The Portal to Texas History, offering a collection of photographs and artwork from the Rayburn family.
The town’s historic two‑story home, where Rayburn lived with his family, remains a key landmark for understanding mid‑20th‑century Texas politics.
